Edit: I feel like I need to add something here. I'm sorry for the "back in my day" that's about to spew forth, but back in my day (I was 18 in 2005) hipster-ism wasn't really a concrete thing. I noticed nowadays that people associate it with a certain style or look, and very specific interests like records. It's weird how it became a sort of stereotype. I mean, the whole flannel and vinyl thing was really only a byproduct of the era. It's not like people were trying to be a hipster. It was a kind of organic thing where people who either had really specific and nerdy interests, or liked weird old shit in an ironic way all realized they had something in common. No original hipster would ever call themselves one, and the whole "philosophy" (if you want to call it that) was about embracing being outside the mainstream. It was never about being trendy. If anything the whole thing got taken over by people trying to be trendy, because the idea of celebrating being "uncool", became cool. It's weird, and this is the first time I've ever really stopped to think about it.
